title: CNI FIB growth causing scheduler starvation + etcd lease jitter - diagnostic notes
body:
Summary:

Short: On 2026-02-18 (UTC) we observed intermittent pod scheduling starvation in k8s clusters in us-west-2. Symptoms included long pending times for small stateless pods, kube-scheduler CPU spikes, kube-proxy conntrack churn, and a correlated increase in node kubelet OOM/kubelet restarts. Root-cause appears to be an unbounded growth in the CNI FIB (route/endpoint table) on a subset of nodes combined with an etcd leader lease jitter that amplified API server latency causing the scheduler to requeue and stall.

This doc records timeline, evidence, live-debug commands used, temporary mitigations, and follow-ups/next steps (runbook updates).

Timeline (rough):
- 2026-02-18 02:07 UTC: Pager fired — many small POD_CREATE latency alerts from routing-team service.
- 02:10: first oncall (Kyle) sees scheduler queued backlog > 400 pending pods across cluster.
- 02:12: kube-scheduler CPU shot from 0.6 -> 3.8 on control-plane nodes.
- 02:15: Noticed increased kube-proxy logs and conntrack rejects on nodes hosting many endpoints.
- 02:22: etcd leader rotated twice within 2 minutes; observed GRPC deadline exceeded spikes in apiserver logs.
- 02:35: applied emergency mitigation: cordon & drain 2 most affected nodes with FIB growth.
- 03:00: scheduling backlog decreased to baseline.

Observations & evidence:
- Node metrics (node-exporter): 
  - netstat conntrack count increased 3x on affected nodes.
  - iptables/nf_conntrack shows many TIME_WAIT / entries related to pod IPs.
- kube-proxy logs contained frequent errors: 
  - "failed to ensure rules: write iptables: resource temporarily unavailable" plus rate-limit exceed warnings.
- CNI dataplane (CNId) metric: fib_table_size (custom metric exposed by our cni plugin) grew from ~6k -> 78k entries in 90 minutes on 3 nodes.
- kubelet logs on those nodes show internal GC pressure and recent OOM kill of kubelet-side helper processes.
- apiserver traces reveal 5s+ p95 latencies for list/watch calls during leader transitions.
- etcd logs: frequent compact/defrag activity from automated maintenance job coincident with lease renew attempts; observed several "etcdserver: server is too busy" warnings.

Hypothesis (how pieces fit together):
1) A buggy upstream change in CNI or higher endpoint churn from a canary service produced a runaway creation of dataplane route entries (FIB growth). Each new endpoint adds state into node-level tables and consumes kernel conntrack capacity.
2) Kernel conntrack exhaustion + heavy iptables rewrites slow kube-proxy and cause per-node API churn as kube-proxy retries, which increases apiserver load.
3) etcd experienced compaction/defrag and leader jitter (likely exacerbated by increased control-plane load), increasing list/watch latency.
4) Scheduler depends on timely node/pod watches (apiserver); elevated apiserver latencies caused the scheduler to retry more aggressively, consuming CPU and falling behind, creating the observed backlog.

Commands & data pulled during oncall (for reproducibility):
- top/ps checks on scheduler: top -b -n1 | grep kube-scheduler- kubectl -n kube-system logs -l component=kube-scheduler --tail=200- node conntrack: sudo conntrack -L | wc -l (or for older kernels /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count)- iptables table size: sudo iptables-save | wc -l- CNI plugin debug endpoint: curl -s localhost:15020/metrics | grep fib_table_size- etcd health: ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=https://etcd0:2379 endpoint status --write-out=table- apiserver trace: grep "list.*watch" /var/log/kube-apiserver.log | sed -n '1,200p'

Temporary mitigation applied during incident (ordered):
1) Isolate worst nodes: cordon + drain 3 nodes (kubeadm drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data) to remove high-FIB nodes from rotation. This dropped local kernel pressure quickly and returned node stability.
2) Increased conntrack max on affected nodes as immediate stopgap: sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=200000. This prevented immediate conntrack rejects while we drained.
3) Disabled noisy canary deployment (svc/canary-spike) suspected of causing endpoint churn — rolled back last deploy.
4) Post-drain, restarted kube-proxy as a last step (systemctl restart kube-proxy) on recovered nodes to flush iptables ephemeral inconsistencies.

What worked / what didn't:
- Draining nodes and increasing conntrack limit gave quick relief.
- Rolling back canary stopped growth, suggests correlation (not definitive causation).
- Restarting kube-proxy was low-friction and safe once node pressure reduced.
- ETCD compaction schedule: we realized automated defrag/compact runs were aligned with our traffic spike windows; disabling the maintenance job during high-traffic windows would help, but it's a deeper platform-level policy decision.

Root cause assessment (current best):
Primary: excessive endpoint/route churn leading to CNI FIB growth on subset of nodes (likely a misbehaving service + CNI memory-usage pattern).
Secondary/contributing: etcd maintenance (compaction/defrag) + leader jitter during crisis causing apiserver/list latency spikes, amplifying scheduler pressure. Kernel conntrack limits and kube-proxy iptables rewrite contention turned a medium-scale issue into a cluster-wide scheduling stall.

Immediate follow-ups (must-do in next 72h):
- [SRE-7891] Stabilize the canary: rollback + temporary disable auto-rollout for svc/canary-spike until root cause is nailed. Owner: Jin Woo. Due: 2026-02-22.
- Audit CNI metric ingestion to add alert on fib_table_size > 20k for any single node. Owner: Kyle. Due: 2026-02-24.
- Tune conntrack defaults in our node bootstrap cloud-init for all prod+staging nodes: set nf_conntrack_max to 150k and document tradeoffs. Owner: infra-team. Due: 2026-02-27.
- Add a preemptive kube-proxy restart/iptables sanity-check in the node-reimage playbook when fib_table_size > threshold. Owner: platform-engineering. Due: 2026-03-03.
- Investigate etcd maintenance job schedule: move defrag/compact to off-peak and add runbook to pause during spikes. Owner: eng-database. Due: 2026-03-05.

Longer-term/engineering work (backlog items):
- Improve CNI plugin memory/GC heuristics to cap per-node FIB entries or compress routes. (applied-ml / serving-runtime?)
- Add scheduler-side probe to detect apiserver list/watch degradation earlier and backoff scheduling loops upstream.
- Implement a "node dataplane sanity" admission webhook to throttle massive endpoint additions per deployment to prevent runaway fanout.

Runbook drafts / immediate edits (to commit):
- Oncall playbook: under "kube-scheduler backlog" -> add check for per-node fib_table_size and conntrack usage as first triage step.
- Add explicit steps to cordon/drain suspected nodes and increase conntrack limit as documented above.
- Add guidance for when to disable background etcd maintenance (only if leader rotations > 2 in 5 min AND apiserver p95 list/watch > 2s).

Open questions / unknowns: (notes to self)
- Was the canary the root cause or a symptom? Need to reproduce in staging with traffic simulation.
- Why did etcd compaction pick this window? compaction should be spread, maybe cron misfire. Check cluster backup/maintenance logs.
- Are there other deployments that could create similar fanout patterns? run a scan for Services with > 10k endpoints across cluster historically.

Post-incident communication plan:
- Draft a short incident email to product teams (ops@, infra@) summarizing action taken and immediate mitigations (Aisha). Draft due 2026-02-21.
- Schedule a retro with Platform + CNI owners + affected service owners to review the canary and rollout policy. Invite list: Kyle, Jin Woo, Ruth (CNI eng), product owner for canary-spike.

Appendix: useful snippets captured from live debug (redacted):
- conntrack count sample:  78211 -> indicates firewall table almost saturated- kube-proxy error sample: "E022: failed to sync endpoints: write /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max: resource temporarily unavailable"- apiserver trace: "GET /api/v1/endpoints?resourceVersion=0  200  3.4s"

Quick checklist for next oncall encountering a similar symptom:
1) Check scheduler queue: kubectl get pods --all-namespaces --field-selector=status.phase=Pending | wc -l
2) On control-plane: check apiserver p95 list/watch latency from traces/logs
3) Identify nodes with fib growth: query metric `cni_fib_table_size` per node (>10k suspicious)
4) If >10k on a node: cordon & drain, increase conntrack on node, restart kube-proxy after drain
5) If etcd leader rotates >2 times in 10m: contact eng-database and consider pausing defrag jobs

Notes to self: write a small repro harness in staging that creates endpoint churn at scale (simulate a service that rapidly creates/destroys endpoints) — use it to verify CNI behaviour and get reproducible FIB growth.

End of notes.
